fieldValues.title: Reader mode makes our repositories followable with no change to their data
fieldValues.summary: The Readers experiment (srs-lab#32) reads the same data four ways. In Reader mode (one column; a page is a record or note followed by what it anchors, in outline order, each with its first line; walls grouped by kind) srs-programme, muSrs and LiveWyer Insight can be followed page by page from their guide: every overview written for them shows. In srs-web's three columns the same repositories show search results.
evidence: srs-lab readers/ (merged #32), tested with Playwright on five corpora, four modes, no console errors

srs-programme: guide, then roadmap, five phases, Narrative explorations and Research, each with its first line and item count; Research opens on its introduction and threads, a thread on its overview, a part on its evidence
Gaps it exposed: two records share the title 'SemanticOps programme' (the purpose and the settings record); bullet lists in prose render as plain lines; Book mode is long for large sections
fieldValues.body: This is evidence for option A of the exercise on what srs-web should show (a reading view first), and for the claim that the data was never the problem. A reading view needs nothing from the engine beyond outlines, anchors and records, which the CLI and WASM already expose.
